output.answer: As of November 2026, Costco's pending litigation (per its FY2026 Form 10-K, fiscal year ended August 30, 2026) includes: four March 2026 class actions seeking refunds of IEEPA tariffs passed on to members in higher prices (the Gower motion to dismiss was denied July 17, 2026, with appellate review pending); a Washington wage class action, Gray v. Costco, whose class was certified December 12, 2025 with trial set for March 1, 2027; consolidated privacy class actions over pixel trackers on Costco.com (Castillo); remaining opioid-related claims in the national MDL and in state courts; July 2026 deceptive-email class action Jay v. Costco; the Salisbury '100% de Agave' tequila class action; and California wage-and-hour suits (Martin Reyes, Nader PAGA). Recent outcomes: the Zydel email-marketing class action settled for roughly $14 million with final court approval in early October 2026, and a federal judge in Seattle in October 2026 threw out a RICO suit alleging Kirkland Signature tequilas are not 100% agave (plaintiffs plan to appeal). Costco is also a defendant in Lululemon's June 2025 lawsuit accusing it of selling 'knockoff' apparel that infringes Lululemon's patent and trademark rights, and in 2026 consumer class actions over its rotisserie chicken (allegedly containing preservatives despite 'no preservatives' labeling, and salmonella contamination concerns) and over Orgain Organic Protein Powder allegedly containing heavy metals.
caveats: The 10-K's litigation disclosure speaks as of its filing for the fiscal year ended August 30, 2026; case statuses (e.g., the Salisbury tequila motion to dismiss, tariff-case appellate review) may have moved since, and the Seattle Times reports the tequila RICO suit was dismissed in October 2026 with an appeal planned.
Allegations are unproven claims by plaintiffs; Costco denies wrongdoing and called the salmonella claims 'baseless' and the rotisserie-chicken preservatives argument 'fatally flawed.'

The $14 million Zydel email settlement figure comes from news reports on final court approval; Costco's 10-K described the class-wide settlement as 'for an immaterial amount,' and the two characterizations differ.

key_facts.fact: Four class actions filed in March 2026 against Costco seek refunds of IEEPA tariffs passed to members through higher prices: Stockov (N.D. Ill.), Gower (King County Superior Court), Ortiz (D.P.R.), Briggs (W.D. Wash.); Gower's motion to dismiss was denied July 17, 2026 and discretionary appellate review is pending.

In Gray v. Costco (King County Superior Court), a June 2025 class action alleging Costco unlawfully restricted lower-wage workers from second jobs, the court certified a class on December 12, 2025 and trial is set for March 1, 2027.

Costco must pay more than $14 million to resolve the Zydel class action over allegedly misleading marketing emails, covering Washington residents who received the emails from June 2, 2021 to July 7, 2026; King County Judge Janet Helson gave final approval in early October 2026, and Costco denied wrongdoing.

A federal judge in October 2026 threw out the Hagens Berman RICO lawsuit claiming Kirkland Signature tequilas labeled 100% agave were adulterated with non-agave alcohol, deferring to Mexico's exclusive authority; plaintiffs said they intend to appeal.

Two 2025-26 class actions allege Kirkland Signature tequilas labeled '100% de Agave' contain alcohol from non-agave sugars (Salisbury, W.D. Wash., amended March 9, 2026, Costco moved to dismiss April 2026; Glazer, S.D. Fla., dismissed without prejudice).

Lululemon sued Costco in California federal court in June 2025, alleging Costco sells 'knockoff' sweatshirts, jackets and pants that infringe Lululemon's patent and trademark rights in its clothing designs.

Consolidated privacy class actions (Castillo, W.D. Wash.) allege pixel trackers on Costco.com violated Washington and California privacy laws; the court denied Costco's motion to dismiss in substantial part in November 2024, and the related Birdwell case was dismissed with prejudice in March 2026.

Opioid-related litigation: in the national MDL, a claim by a third-party payor in Ohio and actions on behalf of infants born with opioid-related medical conditions in 40 states remain; a Georgia county's federal claim and New York cities' state-court claims are pending; Costco is defending all pending matters.

Three lawsuits were filed against Costco in 2026: two over rotisserie chicken (false 'no preservatives' advertising — the chicken allegedly contains sodium phosphate and carrageenan — and salmonella contamination concerns) and a July 2026 class action claiming Orgain Organic Protein Powder sold at Costco contained heavy metals such as lead up to 67 parts per billion; Costco called the salmonella claims 'baseless' and the preservatives argument 'fatally flawed.'

In July 2026 a class action (Jay v. Costco, King County Superior Court) alleged Costco sent commercial emails with false or misleading 'limited-time' subject lines, violating Washington, Indiana and Maryland email marketing laws.

Wage-and-hour suits pending against Costco include Martin Reyes (California wage class action, on second amended complaint) and Nader PAGA action (stayed November 13, 2025); the Madera wage class action was agreed to be resolved for an immaterial amount subject to court approval, and Howell was dismissed.
Costco states it does not believe any pending litigation will have a material adverse effect on its financial position, results of operations or cash flows.
